excerpt: Compare a ready Dubai property with an off-plan home using timing, inspection, payment obligations and the risks of a first purchase.
introduction:
A ready Dubai home can be inspected before purchase and may suit a buyer who needs to move or let it soon. An off-plan home is bought before completion under a contract and payment schedule, making the project's delivery and the buyer's future cash especially important. The right choice depends on the actual property and your plans.

Compare total cost, timing and evidence on the same basis. The payment example below shows how instalments are distributed across a purchase.
takeaways: Inspect a ready home and review its title, condition, building costs and any existing tenancy.
For off-plan, verify project registration, the payment recipient, contract and handover obligations.
Map all instalments and retain a reserve; a small deposit does not describe the full commitment.

sections.heading: What can you verify before purchase?
sections.body:
A ready apartment lets you inspect the unit, common areas, view, parking and current services. Review the title, seller authority, any mortgage or tenancy, service-charge statement and developer clearance. Its visible condition does not remove the need for a technical inspection or legal checks.

For an off-plan unit, review the registered project, developer, contract, unit plan, specification and construction progress. DLD's [project status enquiry](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/real-estate-project-status-landing/real-estate-project-status/) provides project information; confirm the precise project and the latest status through official channels. A rendering is not evidence of the finished unit.

The [JVC and Arjan area guide](/journal/jvc-vs-arjan-apartment-investment-comparison) shows how location and building-level factors can differ even within the same broad segment.

sections.heading: Compare the complete payment timeline
sections.body:
Imagine an off-plan price of AED 1,000,000 with 20% at booking, 40% during construction and 40% at handover. The amounts are AED 200,000, AED 400,000 and AED 400,000. This payment schedule shows how the instalments add up across the full purchase period. Add registration, financing, furnishing and other applicable costs separately.

The chart shows the three components of that one price. Confirm the dates or construction conditions in the signed agreement, how progress is measured and what happens if a payment is late or handover changes. Keep money available for the full schedule, not only the first instalment.

For a ready home, ask when the deposit, balance, registration and any mortgage funds are due. Compare the two calendars with your income and savings rather than comparing only the initial payment.

sections.heading: Check registration and payment protection
sections.body:
DLD's [project registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-project) describes registration and an escrow account for off-plan sales. Its [FAQs](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/frequently-asked-questions) describe project escrow arrangements and official project-status checks. Verify the account and payment recipient independently for the exact development. Review the contract’s handover and payment terms alongside the regulatory safeguards.

Review the sale agreement, payment milestones, initial registration, completion specification, cancellation and dispute provisions. Ask a qualified adviser about terms you do not understand. Retain the signed documents, official registration evidence and payment receipts.

For a completed property, DLD's [sale registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-sale-registration/) describes the transfer and required documents. Obtain an itemised current quote for the relevant transaction.

sections.heading: Consider use, income and financing
sections.body:
If you need to move soon, check whether a ready unit is vacant and when possession can be given. If it is tenanted, inspect the lease and seek advice on existing rights. A property being complete is not necessarily available for immediate occupation.

An off-plan buyer should plan for rent or other housing costs until handover and allow for a possible delay. A landlord cannot assume rent begins on the advertised completion date; the property must be ready, legally usable and actually let.

Ask lenders about current eligibility, valuation, rates and the financing available for each property. A developer payment plan and a bank mortgage are different obligations. The [Dubai upfront cost guide](/journal/total-upfront-cost-of-buying-property-in-dubai) explains why the initial price payment is only one part of the budget.

sections.heading: Which choice fits your risk and timetable?
sections.body:
List the non-negotiables: move date, maximum total cash, acceptable monthly commitments and required location. A ready unit may meet a near-term move but require immediate repairs or a larger balance. An off-plan schedule may spread price payments but requires confidence in your ability to meet later instalments and manage delivery uncertainty.

Test a delay, a lower bank valuation and an unexpected repair. Compare contractual consequences and the reserve left after each scenario. Do not rely on an assumed capital gain to make the plan affordable.

For an investment, compare recent signed rents and completed sales for genuinely similar ready properties. Future rents and resale prices remain uncertain in either option.

sections.heading: Compare the evidence behind the asking price
sections.body:
For a ready home, seek recent completed sales of similar units and inspect the building's condition and owner costs. Compare floor, area, parking, view and tenancy; an advertised price alone does not show the amount a buyer agreed. Ask how long comparable homes have been offered and whether their terms are genuinely similar.

For an off-plan home, check the specification and schedule against comparable projects, including the timing of every payment. A contribution towards fees or furnishing can have value, but confirm its conditions and the amount you would otherwise pay. Neither a launch incentive nor a payment plan guarantees that the final price is competitive.

sections.heading: Explore current options
sections.body:
Browse the [Aliyas Dubai project collection](/projects?emirate=Dubai) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) with your budget, move date and preferred payment timing. Ask which specific ready or off-plan units are currently available and request their plans, documents and complete written terms.

Verify the property and official requirements before signing or transferring funds.
